begriffe.text: Dichotomy (Dichotomie): a pair of opposite but complementary perspectives on language.
Synchronic (synchron): studying language at one specific point in time.
Diachronic (diachron): studying language change through time; also historical linguistics.
Form (Form): the structure of language – sounds, word forms, sentence patterns.
Function (Funktion): what a form is used for in communication; its purpose.
Applied linguistics (angewandte Sprachwissenschaft): uses linguistic findings to solve real-life problems such as language teaching, translation or speech therapy.
Theoretical linguistics (theoretische Sprachwissenschaft): studies language for its own sake to describe and explain the language system.
Structuralism (Strukturalismus): school of thought going back to Ferdinand de Saussure (~1900); language as a system of signs.
Langue: the abstract language system shared by all members of a speech community (Saussure).
Parole: the concrete usage of language by the individual (Saussure).
Speech community (Sprachgemeinschaft): all people who share the same language system.
Signifié / signified (das Bezeichnete): the concept or mental idea of a sign.
Signifiant / signifier (das Bezeichnende): the sound image of a sign, e.g. /frɒg/.
Arbitrary (arbiträr): there is no natural link between the sound image and the concept; it is a convention.
Formalism (Formalismus): studies language by its form and structure; Jakobson (1920s), Chomsky (1950s/60s).
Language acquisition device, LAD (Spracherwerbsapparat): innate ability to learn language every human is born with (Chomsky).
Universal Grammar (Universalgrammatik): syntactic structures and constraints thought to be universal in human languages and thus innate.
Innate (angeboren): present from birth.
Competence (Kompetenz): a speaker’s unconscious knowledge of the grammar of their language (Chomsky).
Performance (Performanz): the actual use of language in real situations (Chomsky).
Phonology (Phonologie): the study of the sound system of a language – which sounds distinguish meaning.
Morphology (Morphologie): the study of the structure of words.
Syntax (Syntax): the study of the structure of sentences.
Distinctive features (distinktive Merkmale): properties that distinguish sounds, e.g. voiced vs. voiceless (Jakobson).
Prague Linguistic Circle (Prager Linguistikkreis): group founded in 1926 by Jakobson, Trubetzkoy and others.
